articles.title: JSW launches electric CV business; eyes Rs12,000 crore in five to seven years
articles.description: JSW Group has invested Rs2,500 crore in its electric commercial vehicle (ECV) arm JSW Greentech, which is expected to generate revenue of around Rs12,000 crore, said Parth Jindal, MD of JSW Cement and JSW Paints. On Tuesday, JSW Greentech launched its brand Ampstar, under which it will design, manufacture and sell electric buses and trucks in India, marking the conglomerate’s entry into commercial mobility.At the launch in Mumbai, JSW Group Chairman Sajjan Jindal said the move was not just a "commercial decision". “When we decided to enter electric commercial mobility, I saw it as an act of nation-building—moving India’s people and goods on power generated within India, rather than fuel sourced from outside. We cannot control global oil prices. But we can control how much we depend on them,” he said. Jindal said the venture was not being pursued for outsized returns, adding that though the business will be profitable, it will not be a “multibagger”.This is JSW’s second automotive business. It already has a presence in the passenger vehicle (PV) business through a partnership with MG Motor. Apart from that, it is building its own PV business under JSW Motors, and is in talks with the Volkswagen Group for a separate venture in which it wants a majority stake.Tata Motors remains the dominant player in India's ECV market, with a 30.11 percent retail market share in August, ahead of Euler Motors at 18.06 percent and Sany Heavy Industry India at 12.87 percent.Ampstar is starting with a business-to-business (B2B) model, targeting heavy commercial trucks and buses for sectors such as ports, cement and steel; the buses and trucks are expected on roads within the next 30 days. The company is leaning first on demand from within the group before expanding to third-party customers. “I would like to have 100 percent EV within JSW group,” said Parth, at a media roundtable after the launch. The group has a fleet of 17,000 trucks and there’s a “high probability” of converting around 8,000 of those to electric, according to JSW Greentech CEO Sumit Mittal.The electric buses and trucks are being manufactured at a 90-acre plant in Maharashtra’s Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), an automotive manufacturing hub. The plant will have an annual capacity of 15,000 units that’s expandable to 25,000. A new plant will be considered once utilisation at the current site reaches 50-70 percent. Demand is “unlimited”, the problem presently is supply, said Parth.Also Read: How JSW scion Parth Jindal is giving the industrial group a human faceJSW is targeting sales of 500-1,000 units in the next six months. “We have existing contracts of around 500-600 buses. Today there is a PM E-Bus Seva tender for 4,000 buses. We are participating in that. Today, possibly, we’ll sign MoUs that’ll give us another 2,000-3,000 units of orders,” Mittal said.On its pricing strategy for government tenders, Mittal said “we’ve been very reasonable in our bidding strategy because we have a lot of other business as well. We don't want to race to the bottom.”Unlike its PV business, the commercial vehicle business has been built entirely in-house with no partnerships for technology. “We have not got into any technology transfer agreement with any party. We don’t pay any royalty to any company,” Parth said. “We are doing the entire stack ourselves. This gives us a lot of flexibility.”ECVs remain a small fraction (5.18 percent) of India’s CV market as of August, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), held back largely by high upfront costs. A diesel truck costs Rs25 lakh on average, compared to Rs80 lakh to Rs1 crore for a comparable electric variant.JSW’s ECVs will be priced between Rs80 lakh and Rs1 crore, according to Mittal, which is part of the reason why it is starting with a B2B model built around its own and allied industries, where the upfront costs are less of an issue compared to the retail market.Mittal said JSW is targeting a topline of around Rs12,000 crore from the business over the next five to seven years, even as the promoters, he said, are expecting it to come within the next two years.

articles.title: Hariprasad's remarks on PM Modi spark BJP protest, walkout in K'taka council
articles.description: Karnataka Congress Chief and MLC B.K. Hariprasad's statement accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being responsible for the deaths of 800 farmers protesting against the farm laws triggered a strong protest by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members in the Legislative Council on Tuesday. Heated arguments between ruling and Opposition members eventually led to a BJP walkout.The controversy erupted when the Leader of the Opposition in the Council, Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, spoke on the plight of farmers amid drought.While he compared loan waiver measures announced during the former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh-led government with benefits provided under PM Modi's tenure, Hariprasad intervened, saying: "You be quiet; it was Prime Minister Narendra Modi who got 800 farmers killed, who were peacefully protesting."His remarks immediately drew objections from BJP MLCs, who alleged that Hariprasad had used derogatory language against PM Modi. The exchange quickly escalated into a heated argument and disrupted proceedings.BJP MLC C.T. Ravi criticised Hariprasad, alleging that the Congress leader lacked the etiquette to make such remarks against the Prime Minister. Several BJP members demanded that Hariprasad's remarks be removed from the Council's proceedings.Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed intervened to restore order, saying the demand to remove the remarks would be considered. He assured members that if any indecent or unparliamentary word had been used, it would be expunged.Ministers Yathindra Siddaramaiah, Vijayananda Kashappanavar and Ajay Singh defended Hariprasad amid BJP objections. Hariprasad responded by alleging that loan waivers under the BJP government had benefited industrialists rather than farmers, a claim Ravi rejected.As arguments continued, BJP members repeatedly demanded that Hariprasad's remarks be expunged. Chairman Ahmed reiterated that the matter would be examined and appropriate action taken if necessary.Narayanaswamy resumed his speech on drought, but Labour Minister Santhosh Lad intervened, prompting Narayanaswamy to object. He alleged that ruling party members repeatedly interfered with his speech and prevented the Opposition leader from speaking freely.BJP members strongly objected, raised slogans against the Congress government, and staged a walkout from the Council. Following the protest, Chairman Ahmed adjourned the House.The controversy is expected to continue, with BJP members likely to insist that Hariprasad tender an apology for his remarks against PM Modi.

articles.title: Shastri and Krishi Bhawans facing demolition, CPWD sets Sept 30 handover deadline
articles.description: A Central Public Works Department (CPWD) letter dated September 16 states that vacation of the complexes by September 30 is essential to facilitate timely handling over of the site to the executing agency and enable commencement of the construction work as scheduled.
